frontMatter.about:
Quality Rubbers is a dedicated rubber processing and supply company engaged in the sourcing, processing, and distribution of high-quality rubber materials for a wide range of industrial applications. The company focuses on delivering consistent, reliable, and performance-driven rubber products that meet the evolving needs of its customers across various sectors.
With a strong emphasis on quality control, operational efficiency, and customer satisfaction, Quality Rubbers ensures that every stage of processing from raw material handling to final supply—is managed with precision and care. The company is committed to maintaining high standards of product integrity and compliance with applicable quality and safety requirements.
Driven by a culture of continuous improvement and responsible business practices, Quality Rubbers aims to build long-term partnerships with its clients by providing dependable supply solutions and maintaining excellence in service delivery.
To deliver consistently high-quality, contamination-free processed products by combining skilled workforce practices, rigorous quality control at every processing stage, and a genuine commitment to the safety and wellbeing of our people.
- Integrity: We ensure complete transparency and fairness in all our operations, including accurate pricing, grading, and weighing of materials. We maintain a strict commitment to honesty with no underreporting, hidden deductions, or misrepresentation.
- Quality: We are committed to delivering high-quality, contamination-free processed rubber products. Every batch undergoes rigorous testing and quality checks, and any non-conforming material is rejected to ensure product integrity.

frontMatter.purpose:
This handbook sets out the policies, entitlements, and expectations that apply to every person working at Quality Rubbers, from processing workers on the floor to supervisors and office staff. It is not a legal contract of employment but reflects our commitment to a fair, safe, and well-run workplace. When this handbook conflicts with applicable Indian labour law, the law prevails. For any clarification, speak with your department supervisor or contact HR at qualityrubbers99@gmail.com or call the HR helpline at +91 8590274505.
Quality Rubbers recruits, promotes, trains, and manages employees on the basis of merit, skills, and business need alone. We do not discriminate on grounds of gender, caste, religion, age (provided the person meets the minimum statutory age of 18), disability, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
In practice, equal opportunity is implemented through:
- All job openings are internally notified via notice boards at the plant and externally via placement agencies or online job boards. Shortlisting criteria are defined before screening begins and applied uniformly.
- Recruitment for supervisory and key roles is carried out based on defined criteria, with efforts to ensure fairness, inclusivity, and diverse perspectives in the selection process.
- Promotion decisions are made by the department head and HR jointly, with written justification on file. Any employee not selected for a promotion they applied for may request written feedback within 10 working days.
- Workforce-related matters, including employee concerns and training needs, are reviewed periodically by management to support smooth operations and employee development.
Employees are paid in accordance with applicable statutory minimum wage requirements based

chapters.title: Learning and Development
chapters.text:
## Induction Training
All new employees are required to complete a structured induction programme within their first 3–5 working days, prior to undertaking independent responsibilities. The induction is conducted by HR (or Admin) along with the respective supervisor/manager and is designed to ensure familiarity with company operations, safety practices, and quality requirements.
- Day 1 — HR & Workplace Orientation: Overview of employment terms, attendance and payroll processes, statutory enrolments (EPFO/ESIC, where applicable), leave procedures, and introduction to key personnel. A basic facility walkthrough is conducted to familiarize employees with work areas.
- Day 2 — Health & Safety Orientation: Introduction to workplace safety practices relevant to rubber handling and processing activities, including material handling risks, housekeeping requirements, PPE usage (gloves, safety shoes, masks as applicable), and emergency procedures (fire, injury, spill response). Employees acknowledge safety guidelines through a sign-off.
- Day 3 — Quality and Material Handling: Overview of raw rubber sourcing, cleaning and grading processes, identification of contamination (dust, foreign particles, moisture), and basic quality expectations as per customer requirements (e.g., supply standards for tyre manufacturers). Introduction to documentation and traceability practices.
- Day 4 — Operations Training (On-the-Job): Practical, supervised training on assigned tasks such as receiving, sorting, cleaning, storage, or dispatch. Employees are trained on relevant SOPs and safe handling practices specific to their role.
- Day 5 — Conduct and Compliance: Explanation of company code of conduct, ethical practices (including anti-bribery expectations in supplier dealings), basic data confidentiality, and grievance reporting mechanism. Completion of induction checklist and record documentation.
Completion of induction training is recorded through a signed checklist, which is maintained in the employee’s personnel file for compliance and audit purposes.
## Skills Development & Ongoing Training
Quality Rubbers maintains a Training Calendar, published each January, covering mandatory and optional training for all departments. Training hours are tracked in the HR system and form part of the annual appraisal assessment.
## Mandatory training (all employees):
- Safety refresher training: Once per year, minimum 4 hours, covering updated risk assessments, near-miss review, first-aid basics, and PPE maintenance. Attendance is compulsory; employees who miss it must complete a makeup session within 30 days.
- Fire safety and emergency evacuation drill: Twice per year. Timing is unannounced for at least one drill.
## Role-specific training:
- Processing floor operators: Annual safety training conducted by an external safety trainer or qualified safety consultant covering safe material handling, proper use of PPE, spill response procedures (where applicable), and general workplace safety precautions relevant to cleaning and handling activities (minimum 8 hours per year). Periodic refresher/toolbox talks are conducted to reinforce safe practices.
- Quality inspectors and graders: Internal competency training conducted by the Quality Manager using buyer specifications. Training covers product specifications, identification of contamination (moisture, foreign particles), and quality classification using reference samples (minimum 8 hours per year). Competency is assessed periodically by the QC in-charge through evaluation tests and inspection performance checks against defined acceptance criteria.
- Supervisors / team coordinators: On-the-job supervisory training covering basic supervision of operations, workforce coordination, shift management, safety monitoring, and communication with suppliers/customers (minimum 16 hours). Training is completed within 6–12 months of assuming supervisory responsibility, supported by senior management oversight.

chapters.title: Performance Appraisals
chapters.text:
Quality Rubbers operates a structured two-stage appraisal cycle each year:
- Mid-Year Review (July): An informal check-in between the employee and their supervisor. The focus is on progress against targets set at the start of the year, identifying support needed, and adjusting goals if circumstances have changed. No rating is given. A one-page summary is signed by both parties and retained in the HR file.
- Annual Appraisal (March–April): A formal assessment against KPIs defined for each role. Ratings are: Exceptional (5), Exceeds Expectations (4), Meets Expectations (3), Partially Meets Expectations (2), and Needs Improvement (1). Ratings of 1 trigger a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with a 90-day review period.
- Individual Development Plan (IDP): Agreed at the annual appraisal, the IDP identifies up to 3 development goals for the coming year with specific training or on-the-job actions.
An employee who disagrees with their appraisal rating may submit a written objection to HR within 10 working days of receiving their appraisal. HR will arrange a review meeting involving the appraising supervisor, the department head, and HR within 15 working days.

chapters.title: Environmental Responsibility
chapters.text:
Quality Rubbers is committed to environmentally responsible operations in its rubber sorting, cleaning, grading, and handling activities. The company ensures compliance with applicable environmental regulations and promotes safe and responsible workplace practices.
Our environmental policy is displayed at the plant entrance and on the HR notice board. A copy is available from HR on request.
## Waste Management
Quality Rubbers is committed to reducing waste generation, improving recycling, and ensuring responsible disposal of all waste arising from rubber sorting, cleaning, grading, packaging, and office activities.
- All waste generated in the workplace must be properly segregated at source into designated waste containers. Employees must ensure that different types of waste are not mixed and are disposed of in the correct category.
- Operational waste includes rejected rubber material, dust, bark, impurities removed during sorting and cleaning, packaging materials, and general workplace waste. All such waste must be handled and disposed of in a clean and controlled manner.
- Recyclable materials such as paper, cardboard, plastics, and packaging waste are collected periodically and handed over to authorized recyclers or scrap dealers. Non-recyclable waste is disposed of through approved local waste collection systems.
- Waste is collected from operational areas on a regular basis to ensure cleanliness and to avoid accumulation at workstations or storage points. Waste storage areas, where applicable, must be kept clean, covered, and organized.
- Paper consumption is kept under control by encouraging minimal printing and promoting digital communication wherever possible. Employees are expected to avoid unnecessary printing and use paper only when required for operational or external purposes. Double-sided printing is encouraged wherever feasible.
- Employees must support waste reduction practices by using materials responsibly, avoiding unnecessary packaging waste, and maintaining good housekeeping in their work areas.
- Maintaining cleanliness, proper segregation, and responsible disposal of waste is part of daily work responsibility for all employees.
## Energy and Transportation
- Efficient use of processing equipment is an important part of facility operations. Employees working in processing areas are expected to ensure that machines and equipment are used responsibly, avoid unnecessary running of equipment during idle periods, and support smooth workflow across day-to-day operations. This helps maintain operational efficiency, reduce wastage of resources, and ensure consistent output quality.
- The movement of materials in and out of the facility is planned to minimize travel distance and improve vehicle utilization. This helps ensure efficient coordination of material collection and dispatch operations.
- The company provides shared transport facilities to support employee commuting. Employees are encouraged to use these services for safe, convenient, and coordinated travel to and from the workplace. Transport arrangements are communicated through the HR or administration team.
- The company sets an annual target for reduction in kWh consumed per metric tonne of processed output. The current year target and performance against it are displayed on the facility notice board.
## Employee Role in Sustainability
- Switch off lights, fans, and any electrical equipment in your work area when not in use or at the end of your shift.
- Report any water leakage, spillages, or abnormal discharge immediately to your supervisor or the concerned department.
- Ensure that waste, chemical residues, and other materials are disposed of only in the designated collection areas. Do not discard anything outside approved waste handling points.
- Share suggestions for improving efficiency, reducing waste, or conserving resources through the company’s suggestion system (physical or digital, as applicable). All suggestions are reviewed by the management team, and useful contributions are acknowledged.
## Business Ethics & Integrity

chapters.title: Code of Conduct
chapters.text:
Quality Rubbers' reputation depends on the integrity of every person in our organization. The following conduct standards are mandatory for all employees from day one:
- Accurate recording: Every employee involved in weighing, grading, or recording material quantities must ensure their records are accurate. Falsifying any weight record, grade record, or quality test result — even under instruction — is gross misconduct and will result in dismissal and potential legal action.
- Conflict of interest: Employees must disclose in writing to HR if they or a close family member has financial interest in any supplier, customer, contractor, or competitor. Disclosure does not automatically create a problem; undisclosed conflicts do.
- Gifts and hospitality: Employees may not accept cash gifts under any circumstances. Non-cash gifts of a value above ₹500 from any supplier, customer, or contractor must be declared to HR and may not be retained without approval.
- Confidentiality: Pricing, customer names, production data, and supplier terms are confidential. Employees may not share this information outside the company — including on social media — without written authorization from the Managing Director.
- Respect in the workplace: Verbal abuse, physical intimidation, or harassment of any colleague, visitor, or supplier representative is grounds for immediate disciplinary action.
## Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption
Quality Rubbers maintains a zero-tolerance approach to bribery and corruption. This applies to all employees, contractors, and anyone acting on behalf of the company.
- Employees must not offer, promise, or provide any payment, gift, or benefit to any government official, inspector, or authority to obtain or speed up approvals, permits, or other work-related processes. Any such request must be refused and reported immediately through the reporting channels described in Section 6.3 of this Employee Handbook.
- Employees must not offer or accept any unofficial incentives, gifts, or benefits from customers, suppliers, or business partners that are outside approved company practices or formal agreements.
- Any employee who reports a suspected or actual bribery or corruption-related incident in good faith will be protected from any form of retaliation. The company will review such matters appropriately and take necessary action in line with applicable laws and internal procedures.
## Whistleblower Procedure: Corruption & Bribery
Reports of corruption, bribery, or related misconduct may be made through any of the following channels:
- HR helpline (confidential): +91 8590274505— available during business hours. Calls are answered by the HR Manager or Deputy HR Manager only.
- Dedicated email: qualityrubbers99@gmail.com — monitored by the HR Manager and the Managing Director only.
- Sealed envelope: Addressed to the Managing Director, marked 'Confidential – Ethics', placed in the locked box outside the HR office or handed to the Managing Director's PA in a sealed envelope.
Every report received will be acknowledged within 3 working days and a preliminary assessment completed within 15 working days. The identity of the reporter will not be disclosed without their consent, and no retaliatory action will be taken against any employee making a good-faith report.

chapters.title: Whistleblower Procedure: Information Security
chapters.text:
Employees who discover or suspect a data breach, system intrusion, loss of a device containing company data, or misuse of company systems must report it immediately to the IT/Operations Manager at +91 8590274505 or qualityrubbers99@gmail.com. Do not attempt to investigate or resolve the incident yourself, as this may worsen the situation.
The same confidentiality and non-retaliation protections described in Section 6.3 of this Employee Handbook apply to information security reports. All incidents are logged, investigated, and, where legally required, notified to regulatory authorities. A post-incident review is conducted within 30 days of resolution to prevent recurrence.
## Responsible Sourcing and Community Relations
## Our Supplier Relationships
Quality Rubbers works with suppliers who are registered and approved through the company’s supplier onboarding and review process. All suppliers are expected to follow the company’s Supplier Code of Conduct.
- Suppliers must ensure that materials provided to the company are produced in compliance with applicable labour laws and ethical practices, including the prohibition of child labour (persons under 18 years of age).
- Suppliers must ensure fair and lawful working conditions for individuals involved in material handling and related activities, including compliance with applicable wage requirements.
- Materials supplied must be accurately described in terms of weight and quality. Any form of misrepresentation, adulteration, or deliberate falsification is not acceptable and may result in termination of the business relationship.
Supplier performance and compliance are reviewed periodically by the procurement team. The company may also conduct site visits where required to ensure adherence to expected standards.
Employees who become aware of any suspected non-compliance by suppliers are required to report it promptly to the procurement or HR team.
## Community Engagement
Quality Rubbers values its relationship with the local community and aims to contribute positively to the areas where it operates.
- Local employment opportunities: The company encourages employment of candidates from nearby communities, where suitable, to support local participation in the workforce.
- Environmental participation: The company supports and participates in local community initiatives related to cleanliness and environmental awareness, where possible.
- Education support for employees’ children: The company may provide education-related support for employees’ children, subject to internal policy and eligibility criteria. Details are shared by the HR department as applicable.
## No Child Labour or Forced Labour
Quality Rubbers does not employ anyone below the age of 18 in any capacity — on the processing floor, in support functions, or as temporary or contract labour. Age verification (via Aadhaar card or birth certificate) is conducted for every new hire before the offer letter is issued.
We do not use, support, or condone forced labour, bonded labour, or human trafficking anywhere in our business or supply chain. Employees are free to resign with the notice period stipulated in their employment contract. No employee's identity documents are held by the company. Any supplier or labour contractor found to be using child or forced labour will be immediately and permanently disqualified and the matter referred to the appropriate authorities.
## Employee Data
Quality Rubbers collects personal data from employees — including name, address, Aadhaar number, PAN, bank account details, ESI/EPF numbers, health records, and performance records — solely for employment purposes. Our data handling commitments:
- Access control: Personal employee data is accessible only to the HR Manager, payroll officer, and, where required by law, statutory inspectors. Department supervisors do not have routine access to employees' personal records.
- Data retention: Employee records are retained for a minimum of 5 years after separation, as required by labour laws (Factory Records under the Factories Act, wage records under the Minimum Wages Act), and securely destroyed thereafter.
- Third-party sharing: Employee data is shared only with statutory bodies (EPFO, ESIC, tax authorities), the group medical insurer (for enrolment and claims), and the EAP provider. It is never sold or provided to third parties for marketing purposes.
- Employee access: Any employee may request a copy of their personal data held by HR by submitting a written request. Copies are provided within 10 working days.

chapters.title: Grievance & Disciplinary Procedures
chapters.text:
## Raising a Grievance
Any employee who has a complaint about their working conditions, pay, treatment by a supervisor or colleague, or any other employment matter has the right to raise a formal grievance without fear of retaliation.
The grievance process:
- Step 1 — Informal resolution: Raise the matter with your direct supervisor. Most issues are resolved at this stage within 5 working days.
- Step 2 — Formal grievance to HR: If the issue is not resolved informally, or if the grievance is against your supervisor, submit a written grievance to HR (email or paper form). HR will acknowledge receipt within 3 working days, conduct an investigation, and issue a written response within 15 working days.
- Step 3 — Escalation to Managing Director: If the employee is unsatisfied with HR's response, the grievance may be escalated in writing to the Managing Director within 7 working days of receiving HR's response. A final decision will be communicated within 10 working days.
Employees may request to be accompanied by a trusted colleague (not a legal representative) at any formal grievance meeting. All grievance records are confidential and retained for 3 years.
## Disciplinary Process
The disciplinary process is applied consistently and fairly. The severity of action depends on the nature and seriousness of the conduct or performance issue:
- Informal counselling: For first-time minor issues (e.g., repeated lateness, minor safety lapses). A supervisor-level conversation with a note placed in the employee's file. No formal warning issued.
- Written warning: For more serious issues, repeated minor infractions after informal counselling, or a first instance of misconduct (e.g., PPE non-compliance after a prior informal discussion, inaccurate reporting). A written warning is valid for 12 months from the date of issue.
- Final written warning: For serious misconduct or further infractions after a written warning. A final written warning is valid for 12 months and makes clear that any further misconduct may result in termination.
- Termination: Reserved for gross misconduct — including falsification of records, theft, physical assault, deliberate violation of safety systems, or sustained non-performance following a PIP — after a formal inquiry at which the employee is given the right to respond.
No employee is dismissed without a formal inquiry. The employee has the right to be accompanied by a colleague or union representative at any formal disciplinary hearing, to review the evidence against them, and to present their response in writing. The inquiry officer prepares a written finding, which is communicated to the employee within 5 working days of the hearing.
